objective.statement: Learn six words about speed and time: adagietto, largamente, stringendo, alla breve, comodo and rubato.
successCriteria: I know adagietto is rather slow, a little faster than adagio.
I know stringendo means gradually faster and alla breve means two minim beats in a bar.
I know comodo means comfortable and rubato means with some freedom of time.

explanation.text: These six words are about speed and time. Adagietto, largamente and comodo describe how fast or how broad the music is. Stringendo is a change of speed. Alla breve is a sign for a way of counting. Rubato lets the player bend the time. “adagietto” means rather slow, but a little faster than adagio. “largamente” means broadly. “stringendo” means gradually getting faster, pressing on. “alla breve” means two minim beats in a bar (the sign ¢), which usually feels quicker than the written notes look.
“comodo” means comfortable: at an easy, convenient speed. “rubato” means with some freedom of time: the player may push and pull the beat.

Adagietto is rather slow, but a little faster than adagio. Largamente means broadly. Stringendo means gradually getting faster, pressing on. Tempo comodo means at a comfortable speed. Tempo rubato means with some freedom of time, so the player may push and pull the beat for expression.
Alla breve is written as a C with a vertical line through it (¢). It means two minim beats in a bar, so the music usually feels quicker than the notes look.
